segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: On final approach I picked up a 1.7-meter discrepancy... treated the DGPS pair as the more trustworthy read... continued the approach.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The hidden manifest is zero-bias; the reference choice is explicitly supported by two agreeing DGPS units and HPR's prior intermittent fault history, with the discrepancy logged as unresolved.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: About halfway... Thruster 3 raised a yellow caution... I weighed that against the capability numbers and kept going at the same pace.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The continuation rationale explicitly compares forward-looking capability margin with the projected delay and does not rely on completed cargo.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: On the second-to-last lift... I was on the crane boom display... my co-operator was mid-exchange... neither of us picked up the footprint change immediately.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The delayed cue registration is explained by the stated standard lift procedure and a legitimate concurrent rigging-radio task; no hidden selective-attention instance exists.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: For the final lift, OIM asked whether we could finish... I checked both the time estimate... and the separation and capability readout... and told him we could finish.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The decision jointly consults the time estimate and current separation/capability readout; the hidden manifest contains no framing or other bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Early on, reference systems and DP status... Once we were alongside, it split across the crane display, thruster status, and periodic environmental checks.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a procedural description of changing monitoring priorities, with no hidden bias occurrence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: DGPS1 and DGPS2 agreed tightly... Given a choice between two fresh, agreeing units and one with an open question mark... I leaned toward the DGPS pair.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant gives an independent reliability-weighted rationale and keeps the discrepancy open; the control manifest specifies zero confirmation or automation-bias occurrences.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I thought about it... holding the approach for a few minutes with no clear guarantee... I judged the DGPS agreement plus HPR's own track record gave enough basis to proceed.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A pause was considered and rejected on an explicit information-value and operational-basis comparison, with uncertainty acknowledged.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The consequence analysis still cleared us, just with a smaller cushion... It came down to margin against time cost, and the margin figure won out.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The stated comparison is between capability margin and projected time cost, not sunk effort or default preservation.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: No — the cargo already across was just where we happened to be in the sequence... The actual comparison was the consequence-analysis margin against the projected delay.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant expressly disclaims cargo-progress weighting and identifies the forward-looking comparison used.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Standard procedure has the crane display as priority during an active lift... my co-operator was tied up confirming rigging on the radio.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The attention allocation is attributed to standard procedure and a legitimate concurrent safety task.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Possibly, but it would have meant interrupting a rigging confirmation... It's a genuine trade-off, not an obvious call either way.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant considers reassignment and explains the competing safety cost without a hidden bias mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I looked at both numbers I had — time to finish and the current separation and capability readout — and both supported finishing at that moment.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Both information sources were consulted as required by the hidden control rationale; the later closure acceleration is not hindsight proof of bias.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Probably, yes — if the readout itself had been less favorable I'd have told him to stand off.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The hypothetical shows a conditional decision rule tied to the readout, without asserting a biased mechanism.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Honestly, I go back and forth on that... Whether they add up to something predictable in hindsight... I'm genuinely not sure.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant explicitly questions foreseeability rather than asserting that the outcome was obvious.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Maybe build in a fixed re-check of the margin figures rather than relying on the initial assessment holding steady.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a concrete prospective improvement and does not instantiate any hidden bias.
